record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Does every chiral polytope have a minimal regular cover, meaning a regular polytope that admits a flag action onto it and is covered in this way by every other regular cover?

evidence.quote: Problem 4 Does every chiral polytope have a minimal regular cover?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P (with a least and greatest element) whose elements are called faces, organized into ranks -1, 0, 1, ..., n, satisfying the standard diamond and strong flag-connectivity conditions; a flag of P is a maximal chain. The automorphism group Aut(P) acts freely on the set of flags. The polytope P is called regular if Aut(P) acts transitively on flags, and chiral if Aut(P) has exactly two orbits on flags such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits.

Given polytopes Q and P of the same rank, a covering Q → P is a rank- and incidence-preserving surjection that maps flags onto flags. A regular cover of a chiral polytope P is a regular polytope Q together with a covering Q → P.

Question: Does every chiral abstract polytope P admit a minimal regular cover, i.e., a regular polytope R together with a covering R → P such that, for every regular cover Q → P, the covering Q → P factors through R (so R is covered by every other regular cover of P)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains an active research question. Partial results have been obtained: for example, work by Cunningham–Pellicer and subsequent authors has established sufficient conditions (e.g., when the facets and vertex-figures are regular, or both chiral) under which the smallest regular cover of a chiral polytope is itself a polytope, but a complete answer for all chiral polytopes is not known.

status_evidence.snippet: Chiral polytopes whose smallest regular cover is a polytope
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses when the smallest regular cover of a chiral polytope is itself a polytope, indicating the question remains a topic of ongoing investigation.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems (Appendix C) - Abstract Chiral Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Appendix C lists open problems on abstract chiral polytopes including those on regular covers.
status_evidence.claim: The question of minimal regular covers is listed among open problems in the monograph on abstract chiral polytopes.
